sections.h1: Some workloads are not allowed to leave the building
lead: Regulation, data residency, latency or plain cost can rule out the public cloud for a system. A private cloud gives those workloads self-service and automation without moving them.

p: Design, build and operation of VMware private cloud, including VMware Cloud Foundation, with capacity and licence planning.
Kubernetes platforms on OpenShift for containerised applications, on premises or hosted, with the pipelines that feed them.
Moving workloads from ageing hardware or hypervisors onto the new platform in waves, with rollback at each step.
Private cloud joined to AWS, Azure or Google Cloud so a workload can sit where it belongs and still talk to the rest.
Network segmentation, access control and audit evidence for regulated environments.
Patching, monitoring, capacity reviews and 24/7 support under a service level.
Sort workloads into those that need private hosting and those that do not. Not everything should be on it.
Size compute, storage and network, choose the platform and agree the operating model.
Stand up the platform with infrastructure as code, so it can be rebuilt and audited.
Move workloads in waves, starting with low-risk systems.
Run it, or hand it to your team with documentation and training.
A private cloud is sized in advance. If demand is spiky or hard to forecast, public cloud or a hybrid burst model may cost less and fit better.

faq.q: When is private cloud better than public cloud?
a: When data residency or regulation limits where a workload may run, when latency to on-premises systems matters, or when steady, predictable load makes owned capacity cheaper.
VMware suits virtual-machine estates. OpenShift suits container-based applications. Many clients run both, and we advise on where each belongs.

faq.q: Can a private cloud connect to public cloud?
a: Yes. Hybrid designs are common, with the private platform holding regulated data and public cloud taking burst or new workloads.

faq.q: Can you operate it after the build?
a: Yes, under a managed service agreement, or we hand over to your team with documentation.
